argument:
JPMorgan's $21.2bn headline net income materially exceeds $16.9bn excluding significant items, with Visa/equity gains boosting EPS. Average loans up 10% and deposits up 7% demonstrate franchise activity rather than automatically higher risk-adjusted returns. Observed credit costs of $2.5bn require asset-quality context before extrapolating headline profit growth.

CET1, liquidity and detailed loss metrics remain unextracted; these are appropriate bank tests, rather than industrial debt or FCF comparisons. A Fed hike does not prove net-interest-margin expansion because deposit repricing can offset loan yields. Price below SMA-50 with negative MACD and oversold RSI provides no established reversal, even above SMA-200. Capital and credit validation should precede a buy-on-correction thesis.
key_points: Credit costs need loan-quality and capital context.
Rate changes and oversold RSI do not establish banking upside.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's $16.9bn adjusted result is the right anchor, but loan/deposit expansion cannot establish improved returns without CET1, liquidity and credit analysis. The correction is not a demonstrated opportunity simply because the franchise remains profitable.
